source: NCERT Class VIII, Our Pasts III, History Ch. 2.

sections.heading: 1. The East India Company Arrives
points: The **English East India Company (EIC)** got a **charter from Queen Elizabeth I (1600)** to trade in the East.
It set up **factories (trading posts)** at **Surat, Madras, Bombay and Calcutta**.
Rivalry with the **Portuguese, Dutch and French** (esp. the French at Pondicherry) led to fortified settlements and armies.

sections.heading: 2. From Trader to Ruler — Bengal
points: Conflict with the Nawabs of Bengal (**Siraj-ud-Daulah**).
**Battle of Plassey (1757)** — Robert **Clive** defeated Siraj-ud-Daulah (helped by the betrayal of **Mir Jafar**) → the Company's **first major political victory**.
**Battle of Buxar (1764)** — Company defeated the combined forces of the Nawab of Awadh, the Mughal emperor and Mir Qasim.
**1765:** the Company obtained the **Diwani** (right to collect revenue) of **Bengal, Bihar and Orissa** from the Mughal emperor → real power.

sections.heading: 3. Expanding Company Power
points: **Subsidiary Alliance** (Lord **Wellesley**): an Indian ruler had to keep a **British army**, pay for it, not employ other Europeans, and accept a British **Resident** — else lose territory (e.g. Awadh, Hyderabad).
**Doctrine of Lapse** (Lord **Dalhousie**): if a ruler died **without a natural heir**, his kingdom was **annexed** (e.g. **Satara, Jhansi, Nagpur**).
**Tipu Sultan** of Mysore ('Tiger of Mysore') fought four **Anglo-Mysore Wars** (killed 1799 at Seringapatam); the **Marathas** were defeated in **Anglo-Maratha Wars**.
**Awadh** was annexed in **1856** on grounds of 'misgovernment'.

sections.heading: 4. Company Administration
points: The Company divided territory into **Presidencies** (Bengal, Madras, Bombay), each under a **Governor**; the **Governor-General** headed all.
New systems: a **civil service**, a **new army (sepoys)**, and **courts/laws**.
**Warren Hastings** (first Governor-General) and later reforms shaped the administration.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: EIC charter from Queen Elizabeth I, 1600; factories at Surat, Madras, Bombay, Calcutta.
Battle of Plassey 1757 (Clive vs Siraj-ud-Daulah, Mir Jafar's betrayal); Battle of Buxar 1764.
Diwani of Bengal-Bihar-Orissa granted 1765 → revenue power.
Subsidiary Alliance = Wellesley; Doctrine of Lapse = Dalhousie (Satara, Jhansi, Nagpur).
Tipu Sultan (Mysore) killed 1799; Awadh annexed 1856.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Plassey = 1757; Buxar = 1764** — don't swap; **Diwani granted in 1765**.
**Subsidiary Alliance = Wellesley**; **Doctrine of Lapse = Dalhousie**.
**Mir Jafar** betrayed Siraj-ud-Daulah at **Plassey**.
**Tipu Sultan** ('Tiger of Mysore') died in **1799** at Seringapatam.
